title: Category: Marriage and Relationship Education | Institute for Family Studies
gist: This is a bare category-index listing of IFS's 'Marriage and Relationship Education' blog vertical (titles, authors, dates only, no article bodies); its main signal is the topic mix IFS is publishing on in 2026, including a piece specifically studying the prevalence of AI companion use.

themes.theme: IFS editorial focus areas in relationship education

insights.claim: IFS published a piece titled 'Simulated Soulmates: How Common are AI Companions?' (May 19, 2026) by Brian J. Willoughby, Jason S. Carroll, and Michael Toscano, indicating the institute is now researching the prevalence of AI companion use as a relationship phenomenon.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Signals that family-studies researchers now treat AI companion apps as prevalent enough to warrant dedicated prevalence research, an early data point for the growth of AI companionship as a mainstream (not fringe) relational behavior worth tracking for AI/consumer-app investors.
insights.quote: Simulated Soulmates: How Common are AI Companions?

insights.claim: The same author, Jason S. Carroll, published two separate pieces in July 2026 on how materialism harms marriage ('For Love or Money: 2 Ways Materialism Harms Marriage and How to Avoid the Trap' and ''Can't Buy Me Love': Materialism and Marriage'), indicating a sustained editorial emphasis on financial values as a driver of marital instability.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: A recurring research theme (materialism/financial values undermining marriage) that could inform financial-planning or premarital-counseling product angles targeting couples.
insights.quote: For Love or Money: 2 Ways Materialism Harms Marriage and How to Avoid the Trap
insights.locator: listing entries dated July 15 and July 22, 2026

insights.claim: Other recent entries in this IFS vertical cover dating screening ('Rule Number One For Dating: Is This Person Marriageable?' by Harry Benson, Aug 12, 2026), commitment and betrayal (Jason Whiting and D. Scott Sibley, June 2, 2026), financial conflict in marriage (Andrea Gurney, May 13, 2026), and fear of parenthood (Alan J. Hawkins, May 11, 2026).
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Maps the breadth of IFS's practical relationship-education content pipeline (dating screening, betrayal/commitment, money conflict, parenthood anxiety), useful for understanding what family-policy and pop-psychology narratives this source is amplifying.
